decision_view.quality: Good niche industrial quality, but material customer concentration and working-capital cyclicality prevent a high-conviction 'compounder' label.
decision_view.valuation: Not attractively valued at the current quote on verified trailing or guided EBITDA. Current price embeds continued growth and leaves limited protection against margin normalization.
decision_view.canada_buildout: Canadian domicile and some Montreal investment are real, but this is economically a global exporter. H1 2026 U.S. customer revenue was 49.4%; Canada is not separately disclosed and is included in 3.5% 'other Americas.' Germany held 71.6% of disclosed identifiable non-current assets versus 20.8% in Canada.
decision_view.ai_exposure: UNVERIFIED as an actual revenue driver. Issuer filings identify terrestrial and space solar, imaging, optoelectronics, advanced electronics and security applications, but do not disclose AI or data-center sales.
decision_view.portfolio_role: At most a watchlist satellite for specialty-semiconductor/space-solar exposure. It is not a broad Canadian buildout proxy, direct AI infrastructure exposure, or a reserve/house-fund asset.
decision_view.bottom_line: Higher-quality of the two assigned names, but price discipline is essential. Strong backlog and balance-sheet repair are offset by 36% customer concentration, margin compression and negative H1 cash conversion.

multiples.note: All numerator and denominator values converted to USD. Do not use Yahoo's displayed TSX enterprise-value multiples because they mix CAD equity value with USD financials.

conditional_entry_logic.logic: A 12x-14x EV/EBITDA range on verified FY2026 midpoint guidance of US$102.5m, subtracting US$23.655m net debt and translating at 1.4064 CAD/USD, implies roughly C$18.86-C$22.07 per basic share. C$23.67 equals 15x. A higher entry price needs verified post-2026 EBITDA growth, stable margins and renewed positive cash conversion.
conditional_entry_logic.current_price_implication: C$27.52 is above the 12x-15x conditional range and implies about 17.4x guided EBITDA.

bear_case: The 36% customer concentration makes a qualification moat economically double-edged: a delay, insourcing decision or contract repricing can materially hit revenue.

Q2 adjusted gross margin fell 430 basis points and adjusted EBITDA margin fell about 360 basis points despite strong volume growth, showing sensitivity to metal, chemical, maintenance and expansion costs.
H1 growth absorbed US$48.1m of working capital and doubled capex year over year; inventory risk is material if demand or metal prices reverse.
The valuation already capitalizes much of the backlog and FY2026 guidance; a re-rating to 12x-14x would imply meaningful downside without an earnings decline.
AI is narrative optionality rather than disclosed revenue, and the Canadian thesis is weakened by the global customer/asset footprint.
thesis_breakers: Loss, repricing or sustained ordering slowdown at the 36% customer.
Adjusted gross margin remains near or below 30% while bookings/backlog fall, showing that expansion is not translating into returns.
Operating cash flow remains negative after the growth inventory build should normalize.
FY2026 adjusted EBITDA falls below US$100m or net debt rises materially without commensurate qualified capacity growth.
The investment case requires direct AI/data-center sales or primarily Canadian revenue; current evidence supports neither.
benchmark_context: Compared with broad funds or ETN/GEV-style grid and electrical-equipment exposure, VNP is smaller, more concentrated and less directly tied to data-center electrical spending. Compared with EFX-style Canadian industrial exposure, VNP has a more specialized technology/backlog moat but less domestic revenue linkage. Diversified alternatives reduce single-customer and raw-material execution risk.

decision_view.quality: Improving gross margins and positive adjusted EBITDA are encouraging, but current cash economics, customer concentration, capital intensity, dilution and governance concentration make quality unproven.
decision_view.valuation: Unattractive on verified trailing fundamentals: about 24.7x EV/adjusted EBITDA, 60.7x earnings and 3.7x revenue. Amazon warrants are currently out of the money at a US$8.565 strike; if all 13.880m are earned and cash-exercised they would equal 27.8% of Q3 basic shares, or 21.7% of post-issue shares, while bringing about US$118.9m of cash to the company.
decision_view.canada_buildout: Canadian origin, R&D and current assembly do not make this a Canadian-demand play. 96.4% of nine-month revenue came from U.S. customers, while the major capacity build and government financing are in Jamestown, New York.
decision_view.ai_exposure: Optionality, not current sales. ElvaPulse is designed for AI/data centers, but certification is targeted for Q1 calendar 2027 and first deliveries for Q2 calendar 2027; management disclosed discussions rather than orders or revenue.
decision_view.portfolio_role: Speculative watchlist position only after milestones, not a broad buildout proxy, direct current AI beneficiary, or reserve/house-fund asset.
decision_view.bottom_line: Current operations remain overwhelmingly forklift/material-handling batteries. The price requires successful Jamestown commissioning, customer diversification and conversion of uncontracted data-center optionality; the Amazon warrants are an out-of-the-money overhang whose further vesting is linked to purchases and whose exercise would also add cash.

conditional_entry_logic.logic: Before certified ElvaPulse products, disclosed data-center orders and normalized positive free cash flow, a speculative 12x-15x EV/TTM adjusted EBITDA range implies about US$2.34-US$3.06 per basic share after subtracting US$25.181m net debt. Paying more should require evidence that FY2027 EBITDA materially exceeds the trailing US$11.862m and that dilution-adjusted per-share value grows.
conditional_entry_logic.current_price_implication: US$5.35 implies 24.7x trailing adjusted EBITDA before Amazon dilution and therefore prices in a successful capacity/product ramp.

bear_case: Two customers account for 70% of nine-month revenue and 88% in Q3; order pushouts already forced FY2026 guidance down from above US$83m to US$70m-US$73m.
Headline adjusted EBITDA does not translate to cash: nine-month operating plus investing cash use was about US$39.5m and required equity/debt financing.
Jamestown commissioning and ElvaPulse certification create execution, delay, capex and working-capital risks before demand is contracted.
AI/data-center exposure is currently product positioning and discussions. Certification and first delivery targets lie in 2027.

Basic shares rose 18.7% in nine months and 5.4m options remain. Amazon warrants can add another 13.9m shares only if vested/exercised; they are currently out of the money, remaining vesting requires purchases, and cash exercise would add capital, so the risk is future per-share dilution/overhang rather than current basic-share dilution.
Family influence and related-party dealings increase governance risk, though the filing also identifies independent audit/governance committee members.
thesis_breakers: Jamestown cell/module production or ElvaPulse certifications slip materially beyond calendar Q1 2027.
No firm, economically disclosed data-center order emerges before the initial delivery window.
Customer concentration remains above 60% while one or both major customers delay programs.
FY2027 growth requires another equity raise before operating cash flow turns positive.
Gross margin falls back below 30% as mix changes or domestic production ramps.
The thesis depends on Canadian domestic demand; 96.4% of nine-month revenue was U.S. and new manufacturing is in New York.
benchmark_context: Broad funds and ETN/GEV-style electrical/grid companies offer current, diversified exposure to data-center power and grid investment with less binary certification/customer risk. EFX-style Canadian industrial exposure is also economically different: ELVA is a U.S.-customer forklift-battery vendor funding a New York factory. ELVA offers more upside convexity if a new product wins, but much less evidence and far higher dilution/execution risk.
